questions.name: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.text: A healthcare SaaS provider has passed initial launch and is remediating findings from a Well-Architected review. A post-incident review identifies alerting and automatic remediation strategies as the highest-value improvement area. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

answers.text: Centralize application, infrastructure, and audit logs in CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3 with retention, query, and ownership standards
Use AWS Inspector findings without prioritizing critical CVEs
Use Application Load Balancer connection draining set to zero seconds for stateful sessions
Use a single CloudWatch alarm threshold across every workload regardless of baseline

explanations.a: A centralized logging strategy makes operational events searchable and consistent across accounts and services.
explanations.b: Unprioritized findings overwhelm responders; rank by severity and exposure first.
explanations.c: Zero-second draining cuts in-flight requests; allow time for sessions to complete before deregistering.
explanations.d: Thresholds must reflect each workload baseline; uniform thresholds generate noise or miss real anomalies.

Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager, Patch Manager, Automation, and Parameter Store to standardize configuration management

explanations.b: Systems Manager can enforce configuration state and automate operational tasks across fleets.
explanations.c: Public ACLs bypass account-level guardrails; use Block Public Access plus CloudFront with OAC for delivery.
explanations.d: Unmanaged keys lose KMS audit, rotation, and key policy controls; use customer managed CMKs.

answers.text: Use a single-Region multi-AZ deployment as a DR strategy against Region-wide failure
Open all security groups to 0.0.0.0/0 to avoid routing work
Skip multi-AZ for Amazon ElastiCache Redis to lower cost on a critical session store
Use managed failover features such as RDS Multi-AZ, Aurora replicas, DynamoDB global tables, or S3 replication when appropriate

explanations.a: Multi-AZ protects against AZ failure but not Region-wide events; cross-Region designs are required for that.
explanations.b: Open-to-internet security groups expose every service; the correct approach is least-privilege ingress.
explanations.c: Critical session stores need multi-AZ with auto-failover; otherwise an AZ failure logs out all users.
explanations.d: Managed replication and failover features reduce custom reliability burden.

explanations.b: Thresholds must reflect each workload baseline; uniform thresholds generate noise or miss real anomalies.
explanations.c: Consolidated billing rolls up spend; SCPs enforce permission boundaries — they are different controls.
explanations.d: EBS metrics persist across stop/start; idle compute should be stopped or terminated.
